newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Supreme Court upholds Ohio natural gas tax.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Supreme Court upholds Ohio natural gas tax.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Tuesday rejected a challenge by General Motors Corp and upheld an Ohio tax that exempts natural gas bought from local public utilities while taxing other natural gas purchases.
General Motors had argued that the tax unfairly discriminates against interstate commerce in violation of the U.S. Constitution.
But the high court, by an 8-1 vote, said Ohio's differing treatment of natural gas sales by local public utilities and independent marketers does not violate the Constitution.

The state's 63-year old law exempted natural gas sold by local public utilities from a sales and use tax. GM argued that the law discriminated against sales by marketers, including out-of-state marketers, and impeded interstate trade.
